After, npm run build type-checks and builds the app, the built page shows the Ada trial heading that React draws, npm test runs Vitest with coverage, and npm run test:e2e builds, serves and tests the app in Chromium. Closed the run check's 3 gaps by writing again the key tests TC-1, TC-3 and TC-4 and their helper under test/coverage, which were missing from the work folder. Ran the existing tests first, then TC-1 to TC-5, then the added checks TC-6 to TC-12, then the walkthrough.

decisions: Finding, medium, confirmed in code, high confidence: the CI coverage step runs the pull request's own scripts/patch-coverage.mjs while a token that can write commit statuses is in its env (.github/workflows/ci.yml lines 57 and 64). Anyone with push access could post any status, including a passing required check. Who notices: no one, until a forged status passes. Users take this path on every same-repo pull request. Not tested on the running app because the workflow runs only on GitHub

Finding, low, confirmed by TC-8, high confidence: with npm's legacy peer setting the unit tests cannot load (Cannot find package @testing-library/dom), because package.json does not list it. A developer with that npm setting sees the unit run fail. The default npm ci path works

Finding, low, confirmed by TC-6, high confidence: the unit run prints a React act warning from the main entry test, whose React root is never unmounted. Developers see it in verbose output only. All tests pass
Finding, low, confirmed by TC-7, high confidence: npm run test:e2e builds the app again after npm run build, so CI builds twice and the browser step is slower. Results are right

Finding, low, unconfirmed (read in code, not reachable here): on a fork pull request the coverage status write fails with a read-only token, so the coverage-status job goes red for a reason that is not the code (ci.yml line 68)
Finding, low, read in code: coverage/lcov.info is written by the pull request's own code, so the coverage/patch status is self-reported. It should not be a required check (ci.yml line 36)
Finding, low, read in code: the CI actions are pinned to the movable v4 tag next to a statuses write token (ci.yml line 15)

Finding, low, design or repo gap: the project .gitignore line coverage/ also matches test/coverage/, where the brief puts key tests. This likely explains why the earlier attempt's TC-1, TC-3 and TC-4 did not reach the test branch, and it may drop them again
uncertain: Whether the key tests under test/coverage reach the test branch this time, given the coverage/ line in .gitignore. A person may need to add an exception such as !test/coverage/ to .gitignore. That is outside my allowed paths
Whether the medium security finding on ci.yml line 64 should be fixed in this Deliverable or a new one: the QA person decides
The run_id field is left out, as the brief gives no run id

suggested_follow_ups: Run scripts/patch-coverage.mjs from the base branch, or keep GH_TOKEN out of its step, in .github/workflows/ci.yml
Unmount the React root in the main entry test in src/App.test.tsx
Let the Playwright web server skip the build when CI has already built, in playwright.config.ts
Add !test/coverage/ to .gitignore so the coverage tests are kept
